svg.title: Where each net's goalie stops a low shot, NHL '94 Genesis
svg.text: Where each net's goalie stops a low shot (NHL '94 Genesis, ready stance)
The goalie standing still 19 out, facing the shooter; both nets drawn as the top one (the bottom flipped top to bottom). Low shot = height 5 or less.
The game's rule each frame: within 8 of the blade it's stopped; 8-14 from the blade it passes and his body isn't checked; anywhere else, his body decides.
Stopped across the mouth: top 72%, bottom 75%
Stopped across the mouth: top 60%, bottom 55%
Stopped across the mouth: top 55%, bottom 51%
Strips: darker = more of the low shots aimed at that point stopped. "Only one": a gap of 5+ points,
blue where the top goalie stops more, orange where the bottom one does.
Turned to the right, the bottom goalie's blade sits 4 to his right instead of 11: low shots aimed 2 to 4 right of centre beat him every time; the top goalie stops them all.
Turned to the left, his blade is almost level with his body (1 out instead of 7): low shots aimed just left of centre (0 to 2) beat him; the top goalie stops them.
Square to the shot, the bottom goalie is the better one, near the right post (12 to 16). A still goalie and low shots only; in play the computer goalie moves (replays: 1.03 -> 1.00 mirrored).
